security_concerns.title: Literal recognition can exhaust memory below both byte limits
security_concerns.evidence: Bounded, offline subprocess probes called admit_text('[{"rawOutput":{"base64":0}},' + '0,' * n + ']', spellcheck=False). At n=20000, 40029 input bytes used 39892 KiB peak RSS; at n=60000, 120029 bytes used 79488 KiB. At n=120000, only 240029 bytes, admit_text raised an uncaught MemoryError under a 128 MiB address-space cap. Each child had CPU limits of 3/4 seconds, a six-second alarm, and an eight-second parent timeout.
security_concerns.impact: The new direct ast.literal_eval path allocates an AST before enforcing any structural allocation budget. This input fits even the 256 KiB tool-string limit; treating that string as one node does not protect the parser. MemoryError also escapes admission's exception handling. The 8 MiB source cap therefore does not provide a safe resource boundary.
security_concerns.requested_change: Enforce a bounded token/node/allocation budget before AST construction, including on the JavaScript compatibility path. Return an explicit unsupported resource outcome without relying solely on catching MemoryError. Add guarded flat-container allocation regressions alongside the repeated-comment performance test.

logic_errors.title: Recognizable truncated transcript families still fall through as indexable prose
logic_errors.evidence: Verified that '{"role":"assistant","content":', '[{"role":"assistant","content":', '{"mapping":{"one":{"message":{"author":{"role":"user"},"content":', and '[{"type":"message","user":"U1","text":' all produce decision='keep', indexable=true, no omissions, and unchanged serialized text. The wrapped control '{"messages":[{"role":"assistant","content":' correctly refuses. A known Claude envelope with type='assistant', 2100 padding characters, and a trailing '"message":' also returns keep because the second identifying field lies beyond the 2048-character prefix.
logic_errors.impact: The malformed recognizer omits shapes recognized by _value_family for complete JSON and can miss existing shapes when their identifying fields cross the prefix boundary. Covered writers can consequently index recognizable incomplete envelopes instead of refusing them.
logic_errors.requested_change: Use bounded, depth-aware structural recognition consistently for complete and truncated message, ChatGPT, Slack, and existing envelope families. Budget exhaustion must not silently authorize raw fallback. Add these cases and late-field cases while retaining positive ordinary-code/configuration controls.

logic_errors.title: Transcript prefix heuristics reject envelope-looking text inside comments and Python strings
logic_errors.evidence: The valid Python literal '[ # {"type":"response_item"}\n {"rawOutput":{"base64":0}}]' passes ast.literal_eval but admission returns archive-only with unparsed_codex. A valid Python triple-string value containing the literal line '{"type":"response_item"}' has the same result. The valid JavaScript '[/* {"type":"response_item"} */ {"rawOutput":{"base64":0}}];' also returns archive-only/unparsed_codex; Node --check confirmed its syntax without executing it.
logic_errors.impact: The raw prefix regex treats comments and quoted source data as transcript structure before the complete-literal preservation probe can help. This leaves valid Python triple-string examples and JavaScript literal examples nonindexable despite the second fix.
logic_errors.requested_change: Make envelope recognition aware of lexical boundaries and structural depth so comment/string contents cannot supply envelope fields. Keep actual recognized root transcript envelopes fail-closed; do not simply allow all complete Python literals ahead of those guards. Add comment and triple-string cross-controls.

logic_errors.title: Valid JavaScript literals remain falsely classified as malformed transport
logic_errors.evidence: Both '[{"rawOutput":{"base64":0}, 日本語:"useful"}];' and '[{"rawOutput":{"base64":`documented literal`}}];' passed Node --check. admit_text returned archive-only with malformed_transport/no_useful_content for both, and _format_tool_result returned an empty string. The tokenizer splits the multi-character Unicode identifier and does not recognize template-string literals.
logic_errors.impact: Useful source examples are discarded because transport-related field names trigger a recognizer that does not cover otherwise valid literal syntax. Multilingual prose support does not protect multilingual JavaScript property names.
logic_errors.requested_change: Extend the bounded, non-executing source-literal recognizer to handle Unicode identifiers and template literals, or otherwise avoid treating unsupported valid source syntax as sufficient evidence of malformed transport. Add admission, formatting, and writer-preservation regressions for these examples.

logic_errors.title: Fence tracking deletes literal source data inside valid Markdown fences
logic_errors.evidence:
With blob=base64.b64encode(bytes(range(256))*12).decode(), admission of '````markdown
```text
' + blob + '
```
````' returned sanitize and opaque_line=1, deleting blob even though it remains inside the four-backtick fence. The same deletion occurs for '```text
~~~
' + blob + '
```': a tilde line incorrectly closes the backtick fence.
logic_errors.impact: Toggling one boolean for every backtick/tilde-looking line corrupts legitimate fenced documentation and literal source data, contradicting the promise to omit these spans only outside code fences.
logic_errors.requested_change: Track the opening fence character and run length. Only a valid matching closing fence may leave fenced mode; shorter nested runs and the other delimiter character must remain literal content. Add nested-length and mixed-delimiter preservation tests.

suggestions.recommendation: Keep the already disclosed accepted-replacement delete-before-write behavior and uncovered writers labeled as deployment blockers, not newly introduced findings. This failed publication review does not supersede those blockers.

Preserve the distinction between the parent's selected integration results, the hypothesis-blocked whole-suite collection, and the separately requested authentication-blocked Claude review. These independent bounded probes are not a whole-suite run or that Claude review.

summary: FAIL. Read the complete 3387-line, 18-section frozen patch. Its 135361-byte size and SHA256 match; HEAD matches the release base, and all 18 source fingerprints matched before and after review. Bounded offline probes verified memory exhaustion, malformed-envelope fallback gaps, valid-source refusals, and fenced-data deletion. Positive spot checks passed for literal omission markers, joined omission provenance, UTF-8 tool caps, the original triple-string regression, and the former repeated-comment quadratic reproducer. Admission uses literal parsing, not source execution. No files were written by this reviewer; no credentials, network, services, models, or MCP endpoints were accessed. Publication and deployment are not approved.
